title: The Sharpers, the Banker, and the Donkey
summary: Three clever sharpers in Baghdad resolved to swindle an affluent currency banker—a shroff—named Abu Mansur, who was renowned for his scrupulous bookkeeping.
keywords: tale of the sharpers with the shroff and the ass
full_text:
Three clever sharpers in Baghdad resolved to swindle an affluent currency banker—a shroff—named Abu Mansur, who was renowned for his scrupulous bookkeeping.

The sharpers purchased an old donkey, dyed its ears white with chalk, and led it to the banker’s counting-house, claiming: 'O shroff, this is an extraordinary royal donkey that was trained in the palace of the Emperor of Hind to detect counterfeit coin; whenever a false coin is placed upon the counter, the beast brays!'

The banker looked at the chalk-eared donkey with a sarcastic smile: 'Indeed? Let us test this wondrous beast!'

The first sharper secretly pressed a pebble into the donkey’s ear, causing the animal to bray loudly as a false coin was laid down!

The sharpers demanded two hundred gold dinars for the magical beast.

The banker nodded: 'I will buy the donkey on one business condition: sign this legal ledger receipt with your full names, addresses, and finger-prints, guaranteeing that if the beast fails to bray at a false coin tomorrow in the presence of the Chief Magistrate, you will repay four hundred dinars!'

The sharpers, terrified of signing their real names before the law, hesitated, glanced at each other, and tried to stammer excuses.

The banker called out: 'Watchmen! Seize these horse-dyers!'

The three sharpers abandoned the donkey and fled down the alley, leaving the banker to laugh at how easily a simple ledger receipt disperses the most elaborate fraud.
moral: Rigid adherence to verified receipts and careful accounting defeats the most elaborate fraud.
